init.title: Reimbursement tariff
init.description:
**Optional: home charging reimbursement tariff**

Why it's useful: on many accounts the EVC-net portal doesn't show the reimbursement rate (€/kWh) you get paid for charging at home. The 50five mobile API does, so Home Assistant can calculate your reimbursement and use it in energy management.

**Risks — read before enabling:**
- It isn't an official public API. It's the server behind the 50five app (run by Plugz) and can change or stop working without notice.
- Your saved EVC-net email and password are sent to the address below. The prefilled address is the 50five app's production server; only change it to one you trust.
- Portal login, 2FA and charger control aren't affected. If the API fails, only the tariff sensors become unknown.

**VAT and invoices:** with the API on, the integration also reads your monthly reimbursement invoices. It takes the VAT rate from the latest invoice automatically and adds sensors for the last invoice, the rate actually paid per kWh and the total paid this year. Only turn on a fixed VAT rate below if the automatic rate is wrong for you.

You can change these settings later under **Configure**. They apply to all chargers in this account.

data.reimbursement_vat_enabled: Override VAT with a fixed rate

data_description.mobile_reimbursement_enabled: Sends your EVC-net email and password to the address below to read the tariff.
data_description.mobile_reimbursement_endpoint: HTTPS address ending in /graphql. Prefilled with the 50five app's production server.
data_description.reimbursement_vat_enabled: Off: VAT comes from your latest reimbursement invoice. On: always use the rate below.
data_description.reimbursement_vat_percent: Only used when the override is on. Use the rate on your reimbursement statement.

error.invalid_mobile_endpoint: Enter an HTTPS address ending in /graphql, without credentials, query or fragment.
